rubrics.justification: It correctly echoes the provided 2BA grade, but overstates image-specific certainty and includes questionable claims such as a clearly well-defined blastocoel and appropriate zona thickness; the image appears somewhat collapsed/early and detailed TE uniformity or clear cell boundaries are not confidently visible.
It integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, diagnosis, sperm quality, and first-cycle status with embryo quality reasonably well, though some links (especially BMI effects) are overstated.

The structure is logical, but several conclusions are too confident or weakly supported, including strong claims about day-4 superiority, BMI-related implantation reduction, and a quantitatively derived probability without robust basis.

Single embryo transfer in a 26-year-old with a good-quality embryo is guideline-concordant, but recommendations such as routine dual-route progesterone for low BMI, ERA after one failure, and PGT-A in a 26-year-old are not strongly guideline-based.
It provides clear next steps for transfer and contingency planning, but some recommendations are more speculative than evidence-based and would benefit from stronger prioritization.
